claim: Other channel properties such as proton-mediated activation, ion selectivity and conductance were not affected by Q276 mutations.
source: Noticeable, other channel properties such as proton-mediated activation, ion selectivity and conductance were not affected
evidence: This is supported by measurements of pH50A, permeability ratios, and single-channel conductance.

claim: Q276 functions specifically in the desensitization process.
source: indicating that Q276 functions specifically in the desensitization process.
evidence: This is inferred from the selective effects on desensitization without affecting other properties.

claim: Substitutions of L415 and N416 disrupt desensitization by lengthening the opening events.
source: We also show that substitutions of the two residues L415 and N416 located in close proximity to Q276 in the β11- β12 linker also disrupt desensitization by lengthening the opening events
evidence: This is supported by single-channel recordings of L415 and N416 mutants.

claim: For L415 and N416, size of the side chains is an important factor in determining the magnitude of the effects on desensitization: small and large side chains were more effective in disrupting desensitization.
source: and that size of the side chains is also an important factor in determining the magnitude of the effects: small and large side chains were more effective in disrupting desensitization, in a pattern similar to substitutions of Q276.
evidence: This is supported by systematic mutagenesis data for L415 and N416.

claim: Some mutations in the β11-β12 linker modified proton-gating by shifting the pH50A to more acidic range.
source: Contrary to Q276, some mutations in the linker also modified proton-gating namely shifted the pH50A to more acidic range (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The β11-β12 linker participates in transducing conformational changes from the upper ECD to the pore gate during proton-mediated activation.
source: likely owing to the β11- β12 linker participation in transducing conformational changes from the upper ECD to the pore gate during proton-mediated activation.
evidence: This is based on known structural-functional relationships.

claim: The side chain of Q276 operates as a valve that allows or restricts rotation of L415 and N416.
source: To explain the prominent role of Q276 in desensitization and similar functional effects of substitutions in the linker we propose a molecular mechanism for desensitization wherein the side chain of Q276 operates as a valve that allows or restricts rotation of L415 and N416.
evidence: This is the proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: In the proposed mechanism, the pathway of movement of L415 and N416 faces Q276, that is it is inward rather than outwards.
source: In the proposed mechanism, the pathway of movement of L415 and N416 faces Q276 that is it is inward rather than outwards as was originally suggested (Yoder et al., 2018).
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanism, contrasting with a previous suggestion.

claim: The inward configuration of L415 and N416 movement enables transient functional interactions of the three key residues and makes the mechanism highly reliant on their respective sizes.
source: This configuration enables transient functional interactions of the three key residues and makes the mechanism highly reliant on their respective sizes.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic explanation.

claim: A competent valve requires concerted work of the three conserved residues Q276, L415, and N416.
source: A competent valve –one that ensures complete desensitization- requires concerted work of the three conserved residues
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Changing any of Q276, L415, or N416 introduces steric hindrance that leads to a leaky valve manifested as incomplete or absent desensitization.
source: changing any of them introduces steric hindrance that leads to a leaky valve manifested as incomplete or absent desensitization.
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis data and is part of the proposed mechanism.

claim: An inward pathway of the rotation provides a means of locking the valve to prevent back swings during desensitization.
source: An inward pathway of the rotation also provides a means of locking the valve to prevent back swings during desensitization.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic speculation.

claim: Such a block would not be present if the trajectory of L415 and N416 rotation is in the outward direction.
source: Such a block would not be present if the trajectory is in the outward direction.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic reasoning.

claim: The proposed mechanism applies not only to desensitization from the open state but also from pre-open closed states that exist at pH 7.2 to 7.0.
source: This mechanism applies not only to desensitization from the open state but also from pre-open closed states that exist at pH 7.2 to 7.0 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This extends the proposed mechanism to explain SSD.

claim: At pH 7.2 to 7.0, protons bind in average to only one subunit of the trimer or at most two subunits.
source: In this pH range, protons bind in average to only one subunit of the trimer or at most two subunits.
evidence: This is inferred from the pH-dependence of activation and SSD.

claim: At low proton concentrations (pH 7.2-7.0), steric hindrance imposed by non-protonated neighboring subunits may prevent opening of the gate.
source: The protonated subunit(s) may adopt the open conformation or another as yet unknown conformation; however, steric hindrance imposed by non-protonated neighboring subunits may prevent opening of the gate.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why channels don't open at low pH.

claim: At low proton concentrations, there is predominantly asynchronous protonation of subunits leading to SSD rather than channel openings.
source: Thus, at low proton concentrations, there is predominantly asynchronous protonation of subunits leading to SSD rather than channel openings (left loop Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the functional data and kinetic modeling.

claim: At high proton concentrations (pH 6.5–6.0), the three subunits bind protons simultaneously enabling concerted conformational changes of the subunits that lead to channel opening.
source: In contrast, at high proton concentrations (pH 6.5–6.0), the three subunits bind protons simultaneously enabling concerted conformational changes of the subunits that lead to channel opening.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional behavior at different pH values.

claim: Results from trimers with fixed stoichiometry of wild type and Q276G subunits support the notion that asynchronous protonation leads to SSD.
source: Results from trimers with fixed stoichiometry of wild type and Q276G subunits support this notion, as the presence of a single wild type subunit in the hASIC1a channel was sufficient to induce complete SSD.
evidence: This is supported by the concatenated trimer experiments.

claim: The results are consistent with previous reports of mutations and modifications of cysteine substitutions in the β1-β2 and β11-β12 linkers.
source: Overall our results are consistent with previous reports of mutations and modifications of cysteine substitutions in the β1-β2 (Coric et al., 2003) and β11-β12 linkers (Springauf et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previous reports showed mutations in the β1 strand forming the lower palm affect desensitization.
source: in the β1 strand forming the lower palm (Cushman et al., 2007; Roy et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previous reports showed mutations in TM1 affect desensitization.
source: TM1 (Li et al., 2010a)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Previous reports showed mutations in the thumb domain that makes contact with the upper part of TM1 affect desensitization.
source: and even the thumb domain that makes contact with the upper part of TM1 (Krauson and Carattino, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Recent structural and functional data have informed that regions between the Q-valve and the pore undergo the largest conformational changes.
source: Recent structural and functional data have informed that those regions are the ones that undergo the largest conformational changes, and all are located between the Q-valve and the pore
evidence: This is based on recent structural and functional studies.

claim: Regions between the Q-valve and the pore are consistent with transducing conformations to the gate.
source: consistent with transducing conformations to the gate.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional role of these regions.

claim: Experimentally introduced mutations or evolution guided species-specific substitutions in domains between the Q-valve and pore can alter desensitization and even enable sustained currents.
source: Hence, experimentally introduced mutations or evolution guided species-specific substitutions in any of those domains can alter desensitization and even enable sustained currents (as indicated in the kinetic schemes of Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference explaining why mutations in various regions affect desensitization.

claim: Not all channels that have the tried Q276-L415-N416 exhibit identical kinetics of desensitization.
source: This explains why not all channels that have the tried Q276-L415-N416 exhibit identical kinetics of desensitization.
evidence: This is an inference explaining species-specific differences.

claim: This study provides experimental support for the original suggestion that the β11-β12 linker is essential for ASIC1 desensitization.
source: This study provides experimental support for the original suggestion that the β11- β12 linker is essential for ASIC1 desensitization
evidence: This is a summary of how the study relates to previous hypotheses.

claim: This study provides experimental support for the suggestion that the β11-β12 linker disengages the upper and lower ECD.
source: and that it disengages the upper and lower ECD
evidence: This is a summary of how the study relates to previous hypotheses.

claim: The β11-β12 linker does not work alone but needs residue Q276 to keep the linker compressed during desensitization.
source: however, we found that it does not work alone but needs residue Q276 to keep the linker compressed during desensitization.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The study combined insight drawn from structures together with functional analysis of key residues to propose a dedicated and parsimonious mechanism to control desensitization of ASICs.
source: In summary, we combined the insight drawn from the structures together with functional analysis of key residues to propose a dedicated and parsimonious mechanism to control desensitization of ASICs.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's approach and contribution.

claim: Further proof of the Q-valve mechanism could be obtained by structural analysis of the mutant Q276G channel that remains in the proton-induced open conformation for long times.
source: Further proof of this mechanism could be obtained by structural analysis of the mutant Q276G channel that remains in the proton-induced open conformation for long times.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future experiments.

claim: Structural analysis of Q276G could reveal the linker caught in intermediate states as predicted by Q-valve mechanism.
source: Such analysis could reveal the linker caught in intermediate states as predicted by Q-valve mechanism.
evidence: This is a prediction about what future structural studies might show.
